sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il VIX è a 19.45, in rialzo del 2.21% e si avvicina alla soglia 20, segnalando un mercato più difensivo. L'S&P 500 chiude a 7,623.68 con -0.52% e il DXY è a 101.81 (+0.20%), indicando pressione sul risk assets. Il Brent sale a $116.72 (+3.14%) ma l'aumento del prezzo del petrolio è percepito come inflazionistico, contribuendo a un sentiment bearish. La compressione del TLT (81.34, -0.49%) e il rialzo del rendimento 10Y a 4.98% (+0.71%) confermano la tendenza di tassi più alti, rafforzando il bias risk‑off.
sentiment.reason_en: The VIX stands at 19.45, up 2.21%, edging toward the defensive threshold of 20. The S&P 500 closed at 7,623.68, down 0.52%, while the DXY is at 101.81 (+0.20%), adding pressure on risk assets. Brent rose to $116.72 (+3.14%) but the oil spike is viewed as inflationary, feeding a bearish tone. TLT compression (81.34, -0.49%) and the 10Y yield jump to 4.98% (+0.71%) underline higher‑rate expectations, reinforcing a risk‑off sentiment.

market_impact_summary.it: Nella seduta di venerdì i mercati azionari globali hanno registrato ribassi: S&P 500 -0.52%, STOXX 600 -1.13% e EUR/USD -0.15%. Il VIX in aumento (+2.21%) e il TLT in calo (-0.49%) indicano un orientamento bearish, mentre il Brent in forte rialzo (+3.14%) alimenta timori inflazionistici. Il DXY leggermente più forte (+0.20%) penalizza le valute emergenti e gli asset risk‑on. La pressione sui rendimenti (US 10Y a 4.98%) suggerisce una compressione della curva e una possibile continuazione del risk‑off lunedì.
market_impact_summary.en: In Friday's close, global equities slipped: S&P 500 -0.52%, STOXX 600 -1.13% and EUR/USD -0.15%. The rising VIX (+2.21%) and falling TLT (-0.49%) point to a bearish tilt, while Brent's strong gain (+3.14%) fuels inflation concerns. A slightly stronger DXY (+0.20%) weighs on emerging‑market currencies and risk‑on assets. Higher yields (US 10Y at 4.98%) imply curve compression and likely continuation of the risk‑off stance into Monday.

articles.title: PS Events: Reinventing Europe – Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
articles.snippet: When we talk about "reinvention" we often overlook what works, noted WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala in her closing keynote. This is true of the global trading system, which has proven surprisingly resilient in recent years, and of the European economy, which might not have a tech giant to rival those in the US or China, but remains a global trade powerhouse and a leader in science and research. While Europe has much to do to improve its external competitiveness, it must not act from a sense of panic. Instead, it must pursue measured reforms and seize new opportunities, not least closer trade and investment ties with Africa.

articles.title: Who Pays the Fiscal Watchdogs?
articles.snippet: Civil-society oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance, because it enables independent scrutiny long before a default. But given that a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it, global decision-makers must do so using agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments.
